text: {"version":1,"kind":"conversation","reading":"The user asks for a subjective recommendation on which player to build a team around, based on the previously returned per-game stats, not a new data query.","measures":[],"groupBy":[],"display":[],"filters":[],"expectedShape":"scalar","unresolved":[],"provenance":{},"reply":"That's a judgment call rather than something a query can settle, but looking at the numbers we pulled: Russell Westbrook (29.03 pts, 10.14 reb, 10.02 ast per game) is the strongest all-around building block, putting up a near triple-double average, meaning he impacts scoring, rebounding and playmaking every night, which is rare versatility. James Harden scores more (30.08 ppg) and also creates for others (9.79 ast) but rebounds less. LeBron James is the most balanced of the three (28.20/8.76/8.70) with strong marks across all three categories. If you want a single primary engine who can anchor the offense in multiple ways, Westbrook's all-around production makes him the pick; if scoring efficiency and shot creation matter most, Harden is the choice."}
